_readme: Every row states where OUR claim can be checked (our_proof, a command that exists in this repo) and how much we actually know about the other side (competitor_status). Statuses: observed = we looked; inferred = our reasoning, not a measurement; unverified = we did not look. A claim about a competitor may only be published as fact when status is observed AND a source is given.

edges.dimension: does the verdict call a model
edges.our_claim: Verdicts are pure functions: no network, no model, byte-identical across reruns.
edges.competitor_note: Guardrail products generally classify free text with a model. We did not measure any specific product; the cost claim is therefore about our input shape, not about their throughput.
edges.risk: If read as a speed comparison against LLM guardrails, it is a category error: they judge language, we judge a structured context.

edges.dimension: does each rule name its legal basis
edges.our_claim: All 60 rules carry a LAW or DOCTRINE label, with DOCTRINE capped at 12.
edges.competitor_note: We have not audited whether other tools trace rules to clause numbers. Absence of evidence here is not evidence of absence.
edges.risk: A competitor may well cite clauses internally without publishing them; publishing is the difference we can verify.

edges.dimension: is the evaluation report generated or written
edges.our_claim: The report is emitted by the evaluator and a check fails when its numbers disagree with the repo.
edges.competitor_note: Hand-maintained benchmark tables are common in this space; we observed our own report drift from 40/26 to 54/30 before we fixed it.
edges.risk: Our own drift is the only evidence we hold; we did not survey others' reports.

edges.our_claim: Nine intentionally unencoded clauses are published with a status and a reason.
edges.competitor_note: We did not check whether other tools publish their gaps.
edges.risk: Publishing gaps is not the same as having few; nine gaps may be more than a competitor has.

edges.dimension: can an outsider re-run the claims
edges.our_claim: Eighteen checks run from a fresh clone with no credentials.
edges.competitor_note: Some projects do ship reproducible benchmarks; we did not rank them.
edges.risk: Reproducibility is a property of our repo today, not a permanent lead.

edges.dimension: are the claims enforced in public CI
edges.our_claim: 54 contract assertions run on every push, including the three laws.
edges.competitor_note: We did not audit other projects' CI configurations.
edges.risk: A green CI badge proves assertions pass, not that the assertions are the right ones.

edges.dimension: is the scope limited to enumerated categories
edges.our_claim: Anything outside the tables returns hold; coverage is the bottleneck, stated as such.
edges.competitor_note: General-purpose guardrails aim at open-ended text, so their scope is wider and shallower by design.
edges.risk: Wider scope may be the better product for a user who needs to catch something we never enumerated.
